items.title: FIGHT CTA and STARTING IN countdown compete on the same screen
items.what: On the Qualifier pre-bout screen the large gold FIGHT button sits directly above the live 'STARTING IN 2/4' text, both centered over the same lower-third band while the twin sticks are already fully visible underneath.
items.why: In the first seconds of a bout the player cannot tell whether they must tap FIGHT or simply wait; the dual call-to-action creates hesitation and accidental taps on a phone.
items.how: Hide the twin sticks and replace the FIGHT button with a full-width countdown ring or large numeric timer until 0; only then fade in the sticks and enable input. Keep FIGHT only as a skip affordance in the top corner if desired.

items.title: Techniques sheet cuts off mid-list on the design baseline
items.what: The TECHNIQUES overlay (opened via MOVES) ends abruptly after the first 'RIGHT STICK DOWN' header; the final rows are clipped and no scroll track or fade is visible on the 390-wide portrait frame.
items.why: Players cannot see or learn the full move set on the target device, so they never discover half the techniques and the reference screen feels broken.
items.how: Make the sheet body a scrollable flex region with a persistent thin scrollbar or bottom gradient fade, and ensure the last category (RIGHT STICK DOWN) and its moves are fully reachable with thumb scrolling.

items.title: IPPON / win calligraphy covers the decisive impact pose
items.what: On the Spinning Back Kick finish the giant gold 'IPPON HASANABI' text block is centered over the fighters' torsos and heads, hiding the contact spark and the kick extension that just scored.
items.why: The payoff moment is the most shareable and legible frame; covering it with type removes the visual proof of the point and weakens the cinematic hit.
items.how: Move the result lockup to the upper fifth of the frame (above the fighters) or delay its fade-in 0.4 s so the full-body impact pose reads first; keep the type large but out of the character silhouette.

items.title: STANCE / TECHNIQUE legend text is below readable phone size
items.what: The four-direction cheat-sheet pills ('step / jump / crouch', 'back / forward / up / down') sit in a semi-transparent bar whose type is ~10–11 px and low-contrast gold on brown, directly above the sticks.
items.why: New players cannot parse the mapping at a glance while their thumbs are already on the sticks; the legend fails its only job as an always-visible tutorial.
items.how: Raise the legend type to at least 14 px, increase contrast (brighter gold or white), and give each direction a permanent icon-sized glyph beside the word so it remains legible under thumb motion.

items.title: Half-point scores collide with name plates at the top edge
items.what: When HasanAbi leads 2½ the red '2½' sits inside the same dark pill as the name 'HASANABI', causing the numeral and letters to touch and the right-side score cluster to feel cramped against the 30-second timer.
items.why: The score is the primary information a player checks after every exchange; cramped, colliding type makes the lead hard to read at a glance on a notch-phone.
items.how: Give the numeric score its own distinct circular badge (as the timer already has) and keep the name in a separate, wider capsule with a minimum 8 px gap between badge and name.
